standard.title: Develop media production skills
standard.description: develop media production skills throughout the production process to construct representations using media languages and media technologies
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use media technologies and languages to construct representations (AC9AMA6D01). They have not yet developed production skills systematically across the full production process, or used digital tools to expand representational possibilities deliberately.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop media production skills across pre-production, production and post-production, using media languages and technologies to construct increasingly sophisticated representations.

nodes.label: Developing technical media production skills
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop specific technical skills in using media technologies — cameras, sound equipment, editing/animation software — through deliberate practice
nodes.minimum_width: Develop at least one technical skill (e.g. camera operation, sound recording, editing) through deliberate practice; describe what improved and how it affects the representation
nodes.typical_width: Develop technical skills across multiple media technologies through the production process; document skill development and its effect on the quality and intent of representations
wider: Experiment with digital tools including cameras, sound recording, editing, coding and animation software — evaluate how mastery of each tool expands representational possibilities
Experiment with audio effects (sound effects, music, Foley sounds) to construct ambient sound — evaluate how audio construction changes the meaning of a scene
Experiment with story principles (establishing setting, disrupting narrative structure) — evaluate how manipulation of time and structure changes what the work communicates

response_modes.reason: Technical media production skills — camera operation, audio recording, editing — develop through sustained deliberate practice with feedback, not through exposure to more representational contexts. Students who practise specific technical skills repeatedly build genuine technical competence; students who rotate through tools without sustained practice do not.

success_criteria: Develops at least one technical skill with a clear production purpose
Describes what improved and how it affects the representation
Practice is deliberate — connected to a specific skill and improvement goal

nodes.label: Using media languages to construct representations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use media languages deliberately to construct representations of people, places or concepts with intended meaning
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least one media language element (framing, lighting, sound, colour, font) to construct a representation; explain what meaning the choice produces
nodes.typical_width: Use a range of media language elements to construct representations across different genres or platforms; explain how each choice contributes to the intended meaning
wider: Explore how media languages can perpetuate or challenge stereotyping, bias or identity issues — develop representations that deliberately challenge rather than reproduce dominant representations
Construct representations that explore social relationships, power dynamics or sustainability issues — evaluate how media language choices carry ideological weight
Investigate how to create representations of cultural or social groups that are safe, legal, ethical and responsible — develop criteria for evaluating own representational choices

response_modes.reason: Students commonly use media language elements by convention — familiar framing choices, default sound design — without reasoning about what each choice communicates. Working across different representational challenges (identity, power, social issues) forces students to develop deliberate media language selection rather than defaulting to genre conventions.

success_criteria: Uses at least one media language element with a clear representational purpose
Explains what meaning the choice produces — not just describes the choice
Representational choices are deliberate — not just genre conventions applied by default

nodes.label: Expanding representations through emerging technologies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use emerging or extended technologies — AR, VR, green screen, hybrid genre forms — to construct representations that extend beyond conventional media forms
nodes.minimum_width: Experiment with at least one technology or technique beyond conventional media forms (AR/VR, green screen, hybrid genre); describe what representational possibilities it opens
nodes.typical_width: Construct representations using extended or emerging technologies; evaluate how these technologies create possibilities that conventional media cannot; document the production decisions and their effect
wider: Construct fictional versions of everyday spaces using AR/VR or green screen — evaluate how immersive technologies change the audience's relationship to the representation
Combine established genre conventions to create a hybrid production — evaluate how genre hybridity serves representational purposes that single genres cannot
Investigate how digital tools and emerging technologies are changing how representations are made and received — analyse the implications for responsible media practice

response_modes.reason: Students commonly use emerging technologies for novelty without reasoning through what representational purpose they serve. Scaffolding the reasoning — what does this technology allow that conventional media cannot, what representational problem does it solve, does the technology serve the intended meaning — builds purposeful technology use rather than technology for its own sake.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The AR/VR and hybrid genre directions are genuinely rich — they require students to think about what representation means when audiences can inhabit rather than observe a space, and how combining genre conventions creates new expressive possibilities. These are genuinely different problems from conventional production and give advancing students a more expansive understanding of what media arts can do.
success_criteria: Experiments with at least one technology beyond conventional forms
Describes what representational possibilities it opens
Technology use is purposeful — connected to intended meaning, not just novelty
